subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum witnessed the death of a two-headed stone giant at the hands of Duergar, observed Daz deliberately weakening his magic, and chose to intervene with his mace after hearing Zalthir's fists and Thorin's blade strike the giant. He later saw the Duergar shrink to standard size after the giant's death and watched Thorin pray for the dead.
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, “Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue the two-headed stone giant but was overruled by the Duergar, who killed it. He later questioned Duergar about aberrant behavior in the city, learned of increased militia activity due to similar incidents, and was approached by Dorhun and Rihuud, two stone giant apprentices of Stonespeaker Hgraam. He was invited to visit Cairngorm Cavern and granted safe passage by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: Thorin breathes a sigh of relief, “Yes.”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir encountered Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who offered him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for service. He noted Gartokkar’s non-self-inflicted ear notches, observed the Duergar’s authority via a badge, and was told the Keepers use a fire dragon to heat Gracklstugh’s furnaces. The offer expired tomorrow, and refusal would mean future hostility.
source_quote: Gartokkar is a Duergar, and he is literal and misses the sarcasm, “Yes. The Keepers of the Flame tend to the dragon’s needs.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz deliberately weakened his magical bolts during the giant’s battle, observed the Duergar’s flame device, and expressed sarcastic curiosity about the fire dragon used by the Keepers of the Flame. He was intrigued by the dragon’s role in maintaining Gracklstugh’s furnaces.
source_quote: Daz ask while holding down a snigger, “So he’s a lighter?”

subject: two-headed stone giant
fact: A stone giant with two heads was encountered in Grygum. It withstood fire and magic, was targeted for subdual by Thorin and Grygum, but was ultimately killed by Duergar using a flame device. Its body remained standing after death until the Duergar shrunk.
source_quote: But the Giant stands.

subject: stone giant (Dorhun and Rihuud)
fact: Two stone giants, Dorhun and Rihuud, apprentices of Stonespeaker Hgraam, appeared after the first giant’s death. They were taciturn, spoke only after long pauses, confirmed Thorin’s account of Hgraam’s death, and granted him access to Cairngorm Cavern. They were accompanied by Duergar stone guards.
source_quote: The Stone Giant doesn’t smile, “No. But then again, I don’t know many. Who are you?”

subject: stone giant (newly arrived)
fact: A new stone giant, flanked by Duergar armed with curious stone weapons, appeared during Thorin’s conversation with Dorhun. It was silent and observant, its presence signaling ongoing tension between stone giants and Duergar.
source_quote: Another Stone Giant appears, flanked by Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, approached Zalthir and offered him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for service. He used a badge to command other Duergar, referenced the fire dragon Themberchaud, and made a final threat that refusal would result in hostility. He laughed at jokes and was literal-minded.
source_quote: Gartokkar laughs. “ A joke. I have not heard a good joke in so long.”

subject: Duergar patrol
fact: A patrol of Duergar responded to Thorin’s inquiry about aberrant behavior by confirming increased incidents of non-compliant, self-destructive actions among stone giants. They stated the militias’ workload had risen and that no underlying cause was known, though clan leaders might withhold information.
source_quote: We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.

subject: Themberchaud (fire dragon)
fact: Themberchaud is a fire dragon used by the Keepers of the Flame to heat the furnaces of Gracklstugh. It burns stone hot and replaces the need for kindling. It is tended to by Gartokkar and his order, and is considered a vital asset of the Deepking.
source_quote: We use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.

subject: flame device
fact: A tube connected to a bottle on the back of a Duergar, producing a flame at its tip when a lever is pulled. Used to kill the two-headed stone giant. Grygum observed it as a magic concoction lit by a tiny flame.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube.

subject: badge
fact: A device flashed by Gartokkar to command other Duergar to disperse. It demonstrated his authority over the patrol and implied a system of rank or command within the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: Gartokkar flashes a bade of some kind, and the other Duergar move away quickly.

subject: stone weapons
fact: Curious weapons carried by the Duergar accompanying Dorhun and Rihuud. They were distinct from standard arms and suggested a specialized role, possibly ceremonial or defensive, in the interaction between Duergar and stone giants.
source_quote: flanked by Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: A powerful Duergar order led by Gartokkar Xundorn, responsible for tending Themberchaud, the fire dragon that heats Gracklstugh’s furnaces. They are among the most prized advisors to the Deepking and offer safe passage in exchange for service. They value literal communication and are intolerant of non-compliance.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.

subject: Stone Guards
fact: Duergar assigned to escort and guard stone giants, particularly Dorhun and Rihuud. They showed visible disdain for non-Duergar access to city areas, yet obeyed the stone giants’ commands, indicating a tense but structured hierarchy.
source_quote: The dwarf watches how the Duergar gives the Stone Giant the briefest of scowls, showing how much they don’t want to give this non-Duergar permission to visit their city.

subject: Deepking
fact: The ruler of Gracklstugh, whose approval is required for any action taken by the Keepers of the Flame. Gartokkar implied that violating the Deepking’s will would result in imprisonment, and that his authority overrides even his own order’s discretion.
source_quote: As long as you did nothing that the Deepking would disapprove of...

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: A location in the city to which Thorin was invited by Dorhun. It is implied to be a place of significance, possibly tied to the legacy of Stonespeaker Hgraam and the stone giant apprenticeship tradition.
source_quote: I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: A Duergar-dominated city where stone giants are rare and often seen as threats. The city relies on the Keepers of the Flame and Themberchaud for heat, maintains militias to deal with aberrant giants, and enforces strict order under the Deepking’s rule.
source_quote: Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh.

subject: mystery of the stone giant aberrations
fact: Multiple stone giants have exhibited non-compliant, self-destructive behavior, causing increased militia activity. No cause is known, though clan leaders may be withholding information. The phenomenon appears linked to the death of Stonespeaker Hgraam and the arrival of new giants.
source_quote: We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior... And we know of no underlying cause.

subject: Themberchaud’s origin and control
fact: The fire dragon Themberchaud is central to Gracklstugh’s infrastructure, but its origin, nature, and the full extent of the Keepers’ control over it remain unexplained. Its use of stone as fuel and its apparent sentience suggest deeper magical or divine ties.
source_quote: We use a fire dragon that burns stone hot...

subject: Gartokkar’s true motives
fact: Gartokkar’s sudden offer to Zalthir, his emphasis on ‘service,’ and his threat of future hostility suggest an agenda beyond mere recruitment. His laughter at jokes and emotional openness may be a calculated facade.
source_quote: The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.

subject: Dorhun’s invitation to Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Dorhun’s invitation to Thorin, after confirming Hgraam’s death, implies hidden knowledge or a ritual to be performed. The cavern may hold clues to the stone giant aberrations or the fate of the Stonespeaker.
source_quote: Did you kill him?

subject: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The day on which the two-headed stone giant was killed, Thorin received his invitation, Zalthir was offered safe passage, and the new stone giant appeared. It is the focal point of all current events in Grygum.
source_quote: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: death of the two-headed stone giant
fact: The two-headed stone giant was subdued by Thorin and Grygum but killed by Duergar using a flame device. Its body remained standing after death, and its demise triggered the Duergar’s shrinking and Thorin’s prayers.
source_quote: The Duergar, unconvinced by Thorin’s entreaties, kill the giant.

subject: shrinking of the Duergar
fact: After the giant’s death, the Duergar who used the flame device shrank from enlarged size to standard size. This suggests they had been magically augmented for the battle and returned to normal after its completion.
source_quote: *pop* Grygum looks up, and the enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.

subject: Gartokkar’s offer to Zalthir
fact: Gartokkar approached Zalthir and offered safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for service. The offer expired the next day, and refusal would result in hostility. This marked the first direct interaction between Zalthir and the city’s power structure.
source_quote: The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.

subject: Dorhun’s revelation about Hgraam
fact: Dorhun confirmed that Thorin had been present at the death of Stonespeaker Hgraam, a figure of great importance. This revelation linked Thorin to the stone giant aberrations and led to his invitation to Cairngorm Cavern.
source_quote: We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?
